increments.title: Rulings replace stalls in the shared brief and every role page
increments.goal: Every subagent gets the same material-versus-decidable test the session already has: a material question still goes into `questions` and still ends the run, and a decidable one is decided, defaulted and recorded in a new step-return field `rulings` instead.
criteria: The shared brief distinguishes a material question from a decidable one in the same terms the rulebook gives the session: user-visible behaviour, a public contract, the data model, the dependency footprint, or anything irreversible is material; everything else is decidable.
The brief keeps a material question in `questions` and keeps a non-empty `questions` ending the run.
The brief forbids a decidable question in `questions` and requires the agent to pick a default and record it in the step-return field `rulings`.
The brief states that each ruling is one string naming the decision, the reason, and what it costs if the default is wrong, short enough to survive the steering projection.
Every role that produces a step return carries `rulings` in that return, and each role page says so consistently with the brief without restating the rule the brief owns.
The repository suite that guards these pages passes, and it fails if the rule or the field is removed from them.
increments.note: Load-bearing and first: it fixes the definition of `rulings` that everything downstream carries. The workflow plumbing in i2 is unusable until the roles are told to produce the field.

# What gets built

A prose-only change to the shipped pages, plus the greps in `test-repo.sh` that
guard them. Six files change: the shared brief, the five agent pages, and one
repository-developer rule page that this change makes stale. No JavaScript
changes — see "What is deliberately not touched".

## 1. `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md` — the brief owns the rule

**1a. Insert a new section, verbatim, between the end of `## The mutation
standard` (the paragraph ending "is your own page's to say.") and the
`## Your step return` heading. Keep the file's ~78-column wrapping; the tests
collapse newlines before they grep, so where the lines break does not matter.**

    ## Rulings, not stalls

    A question is material when it turns on user-visible behaviour, a public
    contract, the data model, the dependency footprint, or anything
    irreversible. Everything else is decidable.

    A material question goes in `questions`. A decidable one never does: pick
    the default that costs least to undo, carry on, and record it in `rulings`.
    A run parked on a question a default would have settled costs the human a
    day; a wrong default costs a correction they can see and undo.

    Each ruling is one string naming the decision, the reason, and what it
    costs if the default is wrong — short enough to survive the steering
    projection that carries it. Rule on what you would otherwise have asked,
    and on nothing else: the small choices your role makes all day are not
    rulings.

The wording is load-bearing and the suite greps these phrases, so land them as
written: "user-visible behaviour", "a public contract", "the data model", "the
dependency footprint", "irreversible", "decidable", "A material question goes
in `questions`", "A decidable one never does", "record it in `rulings`", "one
string naming the decision, the reason, and what it costs if the default is
wrong", "steering projection". Rewording these breaks the guard even though the
sentence still reads right.

**1b. In `## Your step return`, turn the two-field block into three.** Replace

    Two of those fields mean the same in every role, so no page repeats them:

    - **`questions`** — decisions only the human can make, each answerable without
      opening a file. A non-empty list ends the run, so keep it for those.
    - **`summary`** — one or two sentences a human reads in the chat. It stands on
      its own: name the thing, not the file it is written in.

with

    Three of those fields mean the same in every role, so no page repeats them:

    - **`questions`** — material decisions only the human can make, each
      answerable without opening a file. A non-empty list ends the run, so keep
      it for those.
    - **`rulings`** — the decidable questions you settled yourself, one string
      each.
    - **`summary`** — one or two sentences a human reads in the chat. It stands
      on its own: name the thing, not the file it is written in.

"A non-empty list ends the run, so keep it for those." stays word for word: it
is the sentence criterion 2 asks the brief to keep, and the suite greps it.
The only change to that bullet is the word "material", which is what ties the
field to the section above.

**1c. In `## Your brief`, stop sending every gap to `questions`.** Replace

    Where you need one it does not carry, put the gap in your return's
    `questions` and return; do not go looking for it, and do not guess.

with

    Where you need one it does not carry, do not go looking for it: the test
    below decides whether that gap ends the run as a question or is yours to
    rule on.

Without this edit the brief says the rule twice and the two copies disagree —
the older sentence sends a decidable gap to `questions`, which the new section
forbids.

## 2. The five agent pages — each names `rulings` where it already names `questions`

Every role that produces a step return is one of the five pages in `agents/`.
The two other dispatches in the workflow (`load-state`, `publish`) are
general-purpose agents with no page and no recorded step, so they are out.

None of these pages restates the rule: the brief owns the material-versus-
decidable test and the shape of a ruling, and a page that re-enumerated the
five material categories would be a second copy that drifts. Each page names
the field in the same place it already names `questions`, so the edit is one
line per page.

- `agents/researcher.md`, closing paragraph of "## What you record": replace
  "`questions` and `summary` among them, and the shared brief says what those
  two hold" with "`questions`, `rulings` and `summary` among them, and the
  shared brief says what those three hold".
- `agents/implementer.md`, closing paragraph of "## What you record": the same
  sentence, the same replacement.
- `agents/planner.md`, closing paragraph of "## What you return": replace
  "`questions` among them, and the shared brief says what it holds" with
  "`questions` and `rulings` among them, and the shared brief says what they
  hold".
- `agents/reviewer.md`, "## What you record": add a bullet directly after the
  `questions` bullet and before the `findingCount` one, in that list's style:

      - **`rulings`** — what the shared brief defines it as.

- `agents/test-author.md`, "## What you record": add the same bullet directly
  after the `questions` bullet, at the end of the list.

## 3. Two consistency edits on `agents/implementer.md`

That page currently tells the implementer to park every open decision as a
blocker, which contradicts the brief's new rule that a decidable one is decided
and ruled on. Two words fix it, and the suite pins both:

- Under "## Direct-fix rounds": "Where one turns out to need a decision" becomes
  "Where one turns out to need a material decision".
- Under "## An increment nobody planned": "Where the criteria and the codemap
  leave a real decision open" becomes "leave a material decision open".

Using the brief's word "material" is applying the rule, not restating it; the
page must not list what makes a question material.

## 4. `.claude/rules/agents.md` — the stale count

Under "## What every agent shares" the page says "Two rules bind the session and
the agents alike: English, and the default branch moving only through a merged
pull request." That sentence enumerates the rules that stand in both the
rulebook and the shared brief, and this change adds a third. Replace it with:

    Three rules bind the session and the agents alike: English, the default
    branch moving only through a merged pull request, and the test that decides
    whether a question stops the work.

Leave the rest of the paragraph ("They stand in the rulebook and in the shared
brief… Edit one, edit the other.") untouched.

# Decisions taken, and what was rejected

- **The rule goes in the brief, in its own section, and nowhere else.** The
  repository's own convention (`skills/CLAUDE.md`) is that a rule binding more
  than one agent lives in `agent-brief` and every other page points at it. A
  free-standing heading also gives the suite something stable to grep, the way
  `## The mutation standard` already is guarded.
- **The brief must never use the word "rulebook".** `test-repo.sh` fails if any
  agent page or shipped skill names it, because the rulebook is the session's
  alone. So the brief states the same distinction in its own words; it does not
  cite the rulebook as its source. `rulebook.md` itself is not edited — it
  already carries the rule for the session.
- **Rejected: defining `rulings` inside the `## Your step return` bullets
  alone.** The definition needs three paragraphs (the test, the disposal, the
  shape), and burying them mid-procedure between the field list and the
  announce-yourself instructions would break that section's flow and leave
  nothing greppable.
- **Rejected: putting a number on "short enough".** The projection keeps a
  string of at most 500 characters and a list of at most 50 of them
  (`SMALL_STRING`/`SMALL_LIST` in `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs`).
  Writing 500 into the brief would be a second copy of a constant that lives in
  code, and the brief's own rule is to state a thing once. The qualitative
  sentence plus the phrase "steering projection" is what the criterion asks for.
- **No change is needed to the recorder for `rulings` to reach the index.** The
  projection in `backlog.mjs` keeps any field that is a list of at most 50
  strings of at most 500 characters each, so a `rulings` array survives it
  today, untouched. That is why this increment is prose plus greps only.
- **Rejected: bounding rulings by "every choice you make".** The brief says
  "Rule on what you would otherwise have asked, and on nothing else" so the
  field stays a short list of real decisions instead of a diary — the
  test-author already decides "the small things the plan left open" all day, and
  those are not rulings.

# What is deliberately not touched

- `workflows/agile-loop.js`. Its `PLAN_PAYLOAD`, `TESTS_PAYLOAD`,
  `BUILD_PAYLOAD`, `VERDICT_PAYLOAD` and `CUT_PAYLOAD` lists, its per-role
  schemas and the comment at its line 338 ("`questions` and `summary` mean the
  same in every role") are increment 2's, which names the dispatch prompts and
  the result explicitly. Until it lands, a page says the step return carries
  `rulings` while the dispatch prompt does not name it and the structured schema
  has no such property; that gap is known, deliberate, and closed by i2. Do not
  edit the workflow script here.
- `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs` and its suite — see the projection
  decision above.
- `rulebook.md` — it already carries the rule for the session.
- `README.md` — it names no step-return field.

# Whether

Tests are needed. The change is prose in shipped pages, and this repository
already guards such prose with greps in its own suite — that is exactly what
criterion 6 asks for.

# Where they go, and the suite doc

Every case below is a bash case in `test-repo.sh` at the repository root: no
framework, no runner, just `if … then ok "…" else no "…" fi`. Put them all in
one new section, appended to the end of the existing "=== the mutation standard
has one owner" section — that is, after its last case (the `says? so and why`
grep) and immediately before the `echo "=== a run resumes from the state it
recorded"` block. Open the section the way every other one opens:

    echo
    echo "=== a decidable question gets a ruling, not a stall"

**There is no suite doc for `test-repo.sh` and there must not be one.** Its
conventions are given here instead. Do not create a `CLAUDE.md` at the
repository root: a case already in this same suite fails when one exists,
because a root `CLAUDE.md` loads as project memory and is inherited by every
subagent. Do not create one beside `test-repo.sh` under another name either.
The conventions you need:

- `ok "…"` counts a pass and `no "…"` counts a failure; both take one sentence
  stating the guaranteed fact, lower case, no "should".
- `$root` is the repository root; every path is `"$root/…"`.
- A comment above each case names the criterion it covers and the break — the
  edit that would make it fail. Follow that; the section reads as documentation
  of what may not be deleted.
- A phrase that wraps across lines in a Markdown page is grepped from a
  collapsed copy of the file, the way the reviewer case in the section above
  does it: `page_collapsed="$(tr '\n' ' ' <"$root/…md" | tr -s ' ')"`, then
  `echo "$page_collapsed" | grep -q '…'`. Every phrase below wraps, so collapse
  first — a plain `grep` on the file would miss it.
- An "exactly one page owns this" case builds a path list with
  `grep -lie '…' "$root"/agents/*.md "$root"/skills/*/SKILL.md` and compares the
  whole string to the expected path, printing the list on failure. Copy the
  `mutation_standard_owners` case just above.
- Cases are flat; no functions, no loops except the small `for` loops the file
  already uses over `"$root"/agents/*.md` and over a `declare -a` list of terms.

Collapse `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md` once at the top of the section and reuse
it: `brief_collapsed="$(tr '\n' ' ' <"$root/skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md" | tr -s ' ')"`.

# What: the cases, criterion by criterion

## Criterion 1 — the brief distinguishes material from decidable, in the terms the rulebook gives the session

**Case 1.1 — the five material terms stand in the brief and in `rulebook.md`
alike.** Loop over exactly these five strings: `user-visible behaviour`,
`public contract`, `data model`, `dependency footprint`, `irreversible`. For
each, assert it appears in `$brief_collapsed` and in `$root/rulebook.md`; one
`ok`/`no` per term is fine, or one per file per term. State: no input beyond the
two files. Expected: every term present on both sides. *Break:* delete the
sentence "A question is material when it turns on user-visible behaviour, a
public contract, the data model, the dependency footprint, or anything
irreversible." from the brief — four terms vanish and the case fails. It fails
in the other direction too, if the rulebook's own list is edited away from the
brief's, which is what "in the same terms" means.

**Case 1.2 — the brief names the other side of the test.** Assert
`$brief_collapsed` contains `decidable`. *Break:* delete "Everything else is
decidable." from the brief.

## Criterion 2 — a material question stays in `questions`, and a non-empty `questions` still ends the run

**Case 2.1** — assert `$brief_collapsed` contains the exact phrase
``A material question goes in `questions` ``. *Break:* delete that sentence from
the "Rulings, not stalls" section, or reword it to send a material question
anywhere else.

**Case 2.2** — assert `$brief_collapsed` contains the exact phrase
`A non-empty list ends the run`. *Break:* delete that clause from the
`questions` bullet of "Your step return", which is the only place it stands.

## Criterion 3 — a decidable question is forbidden in `questions`, defaulted, and recorded in `rulings`

**Case 3.1** — assert `$brief_collapsed` contains `A decidable one never does`.
*Break:* delete that sentence, or soften it to allow a decidable question into
`questions`.

**Case 3.2** — assert `$brief_collapsed` contains ``record it in `rulings` ``
and `pick the default`. *Break:* delete either half of "pick the default that
costs least to undo, carry on, and record it in `rulings`".

**Case 3.3** — assert `$brief_collapsed` contains ``- **`rulings`** —``, the
bullet that makes it one of the fields meaning the same in every role. *Break:*
delete that bullet from the "Three of those fields mean the same in every role"
list. Note the collapsed copy squeezes runs of spaces, so match the bullet with
its backticks and the em dash exactly as written, or match the shorter
``**`rulings`**`` if the dash proves awkward to quote in bash.

## Criterion 4 — the shape of one ruling

**Case 4.1** — assert `$brief_collapsed` contains `one string naming the
decision, the reason, and what it costs if the default is wrong` (as one
collapsed line). *Break:* delete or reword that sentence.

**Case 4.2** — assert `$brief_collapsed` contains `steering projection`.
*Break:* drop the length constraint from that sentence.

## Criterion 5 — every role that produces a step return carries `rulings`, and no page restates the rule

**Case 5.1 — every agent page names the field.** Loop over `"$root"/agents/*.md`
the way the existing `missing_backlog_ref` case does; collect the basename of
any page where `grep -q 'rulings'` fails; `ok` when the list is empty, `no`
listing the pages otherwise. There are five pages: `planner.md`,
`researcher.md`, `test-author.md`, `implementer.md`, `reviewer.md`. *Break:*
remove `rulings` from any one of them — the case fails and names it.

**Case 5.2 — the brief is the only page that defines the test.** Build
`ruling_rule_owners="$(grep -lie 'dependency footprint' "$root"/agents/*.md
"$root"/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null || true)"` and assert it equals exactly
`"$root/skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md"`; on failure print the list the way
`mutation_standard_owners` does. *Break, either direction:* restate the material
list on any agent page or second shipped skill (two paths match), or delete it
from the brief (none match).

**Case 5.3 — the implementer no longer parks every open decision.** Collapse
`$root/agents/implementer.md` the same way and assert it contains
`need a material decision` and `leave a material decision open`, and does not
contain the old `leave a real decision open`. *Break:* revert either edit.

## Criterion 6 — the suite that guards these pages passes and goes red when the rule or the field is removed

No case of its own: the criterion is about the section above existing and
biting, and every case names the break that proves it does. Adding a case that
runs `test-repo.sh` from inside `test-repo.sh` would recurse.

# Deliberately untested

- The `.claude/rules/agents.md` edit ("Three rules bind the session and the
  agents alike"). It is a repository-developer note, no criterion of this
  increment covers it, and a grep on its count would break every time a fourth
  such rule appears.
- The exact placement of the new brief section between two headings, and the
  Markdown line wrapping. Neither changes what any agent is told, and the
  collapsed-copy greps are placement-independent on purpose.
- That an agent actually produces a `rulings` list at run time. Nothing in this
  increment executes an agent, and the plumbing that would carry such a list to
  the workflow is increment 2's.

# How, per case

Level: unit, in the sense this repository uses — a static assertion about a file
in the checkout. File: `test-repo.sh`, the only one. Framework: none; bash with
the file's own `ok`/`no` helpers. Command that runs just these cases, and the
whole file, from the repository root:

    bash test-repo.sh

# What counts as done

    bash test-repo.sh

That one command, and nothing else. It exits 0 only when every case in it
passes, and it is the only suite that reads the pages this increment changes.

# What is already red

Nothing was run to find out — no command was run at all while writing this plan,
which is the rule for this step, and a run would have bought no fact a reading
did not already give. The expected state when the tests land first is that every
case in the new section fails (the phrases are not in the pages yet) and every
case already in the file passes; the implementer's run of the command above is
the first one that happens.
return.summary: Planned the material-versus-decidable test as a new "Rulings, not stalls" section of the shared brief, with `rulings` added to its three shared step-return fields and named on all five agent pages, and a new section of grep cases in the repository's own suite that goes red if the rule or the field is deleted. No code changes: the run state's steering projection already carries a list of short strings, so `rulings` survives it untouched, and the workflow plumbing stays with increment 2.

increments.title: The run's rulings reach the human through the result and the pull request
increments.goal: Every ruling any step of a run recorded comes back in the workflow result and is listed under its own heading in the pull-request body, so a decision taken on the human's behalf never reaches them only through `backlog.json`.
criteria: Every role's structured return to the workflow carries its rulings, and the dispatch prompts name `rulings` among the fields the step records.
The workflow result carries every ruling recorded by any step of the run, each traceable to the step that made it.
A resumed run recovers the rulings of steps it skips, so the result of a resumed run is not poorer than that of an uninterrupted one.
The pull-request body lists the run's rulings under their own heading, built from what the workflow already holds and without the publishing agent reading `backlog.json`.
A run with no rulings adds no empty heading and no noise anywhere.
The repository suite covers the collection, the result and the body text, and each of those cases fails if the corresponding behaviour is removed.
